1.translation: After teaching in Chapters 7 and 8 that the Lord’s supreme truth is easily reached only through devotion, Śrīdhara now elaborates His inconceivable glory and the extraordinary power of devotion: “But to you, who do not find fault, I shall declare this most confidential knowledge together with realization. Knowing it, you will be freed from the inauspiciousness of saṃsāra and become liberated immediately.” Among progressively deeper teachings, knowledge of dharma is secret, knowledge of the Self distinct from the body is more secret, and knowledge of the Supreme Self is most secret.
word_for_word: in the seventh and eighth chapters
to one who does not find fault
knowledge of the Self distinct from the body and the rest

2.translation: This knowledge is the royal knowledge, the king among forms of knowledge; the royal secret, the king among what is hidden; supremely purifying; directly apprehended, with its result experienced immediately; righteous, because it is not separate from dharma and contains the fruits of all dharma; very easy to practice; and imperishable, because its fruit does not decay.
word_for_word: because it contains the fruit of all dharma

3.translation: Why, then, are there still people in saṃsāra if this teaching is so easy to practice? Those without faith in this dharma—who do not accept it with the attitude that it is true—even if they strive for attainment of Me by another means, fail to reach Me and return, wandering on the path of death-filled saṃsāra.
word_for_word: not accepting it with an attitude of trust

4.translation: Śrīdhara turns to the knowledge he has introduced: “This entire world is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest form.” As the causal, supersensory reality, I pervade the world; after creating it, I enter it, as scripture says. Therefore all moving and unmoving beings abide in Me, their cause. Yet, like clay in the pots that arise from it, I am not located in those beings as an effect, because I am unattached like space.
word_for_word: and I am not located in them

5.translation: Nor are beings truly located in Me, because I am unattached. One might think that the Lord’s pervasion and His being the support of beings, stated earlier, are contradictory. Śrīdhara answers: behold My extraordinary divine yoga, the wondrous power by which the impossible is made possible; because the splendor of My yoga-māyā cannot be reasoned out, there is no contradiction. Behold another marvel: My Self bears and protects beings, yet in My supreme nature I am not situated in them. A living being holds and protects a body while remaining joined to it through ego; I do so without ego.
word_for_word: nor are beings located in Me
skill in making the impossible possible
the protector and nourisher of beings
because of being free from ego

6.translation: Śrīdhara gives an example of a support that does not become attached to what it supports: just as the great, all-moving air is eternally situated in space because it cannot exist without room, yet does not become joined to space because contact is impossible for what is without parts, so understand that all beings are situated in Me.
word_for_word: the relation of support and what is supported
does not become joined to space

7.translation: The Lord has explained that, though unattached, He supports the world through yoga-māyā; He now states that the same power causes its creation and dissolution: “At the end of a kalpa, all beings enter My nature; at the beginning of a kalpa I send them forth again.” They dissolve into My three-guṇa nature and are projected again at the next creation.
word_for_word: at the end of a kalpa
into māyā consisting of the three guṇas
at the beginning of a kalpa

8.translation: If the Lord is unattached and changeless, how does He create? Śrīdhara answers: taking His own nature, which is under His control, as the basis, He repeatedly sends forth the entire fourfold multitude of beings, which had dissolved and is subject to karma and the rest. He creates them in many forms through the force of prakṛti, shaped by the dispositions produced by previous actions.
word_for_word: having taken as a basis / presided over
subject to karma and the rest
through the force of that disposition

9.translation: If the Lord performs varied actions such as creation, why is He not bound like a living being? Śrīdhara answers: those actions do not bind Me. Attachment to action is the cause of bondage, but because all My desires are fulfilled I have no such attachment. Remaining like an indifferent person, I am not bound by those actions; indeed, agency is not possible for one who remains indifferent.
word_for_word: bondage like that of a living being
